newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs subside on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs subside on profit-taking.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures softened in late Friday trade as players cashed in their gains ahead of the weekend.
Dealers said there was a short squeeze early in the day after the previous session's rally on an unexpected drop in Japan's April industrial production data.
"The market remained quite high in the morning but then profit-taking set in and it was sold down," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said the release of poor unemployment numbers provided some support to the market but players were still keen to sell on any rise.
Comments by a Liberal Democratic Party official that Japan could raise interest rates by early autumn had little impact on the market.
"It looks like the bond dealers just laughed it off. Nobody really believes him," a dealer with another Japanese house said.
"The market thinks rates will not go up in the short term," he said, noting that this week's data supported the view.
The lead December Euroyen contract stood at 98.84 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 98.91, which was also the day high.
"I'm still looking to sell December Euroyen near 98.90 but any dips down to 98.79 should see some buying," the first trader said.
June JGBs settled at 123.97 against their previous 123.58.
Eurodollar futures ended little changed in featureless trade as the market had little to look forward to in the way of key economic data.
